title: Djokovic Comes Back to Win in Beijing
summary:
Novak Djokovic had a tough match at the China Open in Beijing. He lost the first set to China's Bu Yunchaokete. Then he came back to win 4-6, 7-6, 6-2. The match lasted two hours and 52 minutes.

Djokovic is 39 years old. He has won the China Open six times. He has won all 31 matches he has played in Beijing.

In the second set, Djokovic needed a medical timeout. He also spoke with a trainer. He went on to win the tie-break 7-2. Then he won four games in a row in the final set. He finished with a backhand winner.

Next, Djokovic will play either Alexander Zverev or Shang Juncheng for a place in the quarter-finals.

In the women's event, Aryna Sabalenka won her first match. She beat Renata Zarazua 6-1, 6-3. Sabalenka hit 11 aces. The match took 63 minutes.

Sabalenka is the world number two. She said expecting more from herself can help her improve, but it can also use up her energy. She is trying to be easier on herself.

Sabalenka will play Nikola Bartunkova next. Bartunkova is a 20-year-old from the Czech Republic. She came close to beating Sabalenka at the Berlin Open in June.

In other matches, Mirra Andreeva beat Yuan Yue. Daniil Medvedev also won. British doubles pair Julian Cash and Lloyd Glasspool won their match too.
why_it_matters: The matches show how players can recover after a difficult start. Sabalenka's comments also describe how high expectations can both help a player and use up energy.
